{"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-dd28bfe6e12c4306ad03d743853935ac","toolName":"read","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement\n\n> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (item `dg-07`)\n> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`\n> Effort: M\n> Depends on: `dg-03` (isolation posture), `dg-06` (orchestrator obeys router)\n> Related: `symphony/trust-posture-binding` (priority 12) — declaration layer\n\n## Why\n\nThe coordinator has an `isolation` field that means nothing.\n\n`agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py:264` declares\n`VALID_ISOLATION_MODES = {\"worktree\", \"sandbox\", \"none\"}`. The value is schema-validated,\nstored on `AgentEntry`, exposed through `get_agent_isolation()` (`agents_config.py:979`),\nand asserted in `tests/test_agents_config_isolation.py:170` — which pins `codex` to\n`\"sandbox\"`. **No production caller reads it.** An agent declared `isolation: sandbox`\ntoday runs exactly like one declared `isolation: none`.\n\nThree adjacent gaps compound it:\n\n**Worktree isolation is concurrency isolation, not security isolation.** The invariant in\n`docs/guides/worktree-management.md` is rigorously enforced — one agent, one worktree, one\nbranch, guarded by `checkout_policy.py require-mutation`. It stops agents corrupting each\nother's git state. It does not stop a dispatched agent reading `~/.ssh/id_rsa` or POSTing\nthe repository to a pastebin, because a worktree is an ordinary directory owned by the\nordinary uid.\n\n**Network policy is advisory.** `network_policies.py` (90 lines) answers `check_domain()`\nthrough `policy_engine.py:361`. An agent must *voluntarily ask permission*. Nothing\nenforces the answer at the socket. This is the same defect `add-coordinator-llm-gateway`\nnames for spend: *\"that ceiling is advisory — enforced by post-hoc reconciliation, not at\nrequest time.\"* Same shape, different resource.\n\n**Sandbox intent is already expressed, in three incompatible dialects, enforced by nobody.**\n`agents.yaml:60-66` and `:131-137`:\n\n```yaml\nreview:      { args: [\"--print\", \"--allowedTools\", \"Read,Grep,Glob\"] }   # claude\nreview:      { args: [\"exec\", \"-s\", \"read-only\"] }                        # codex\nalternative: { args: [\"exec\", \"-s\", \"workspace-write\"] }\n```\n\nThe file's own header comment says \"the dispatch mode controls sandbox permissions.\" That\nis a policy statement per dispatch mode, written three different ways, enforced by whatever\neach vendor felt like implementing, verifiable by us in no way at all.\n\nMeanwhile `symphony/trust-posture-binding` commits to a posture artifact declaring\n\"sandbox mode, network allowlist\" bound to `policy_engine.py` so posture is\n\"**enforceable, not just documented**.\" There is currently no mechanism that could make\nit enforceable. This change is that mechanism.\n\n### Why now, and why at dispatch\n\nDispatched vendor CLIs are the sharpest edge in the system: `review_dispatcher.py`\nspawns `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` and friends with prompts assembled from repository\ncontent, and every one of them inherits the full ambient authority of the developer's\nuid — SSH keys, cloud credentials, shell rc files, unrestricted egress. That is code we\ndid not write, driven by prompts we do not fully review.\n\nIt is also, conveniently, a single chokepoint. `CliVendorAdapter.build_command()`\n(`review_dispatcher.py:218`) constructs `cmd`; `subprocess.run(cmd, ...)` at `:279` and\n`:521` executes it. One injection site covers every vendor.\n\nThe pressure is increasing, not static. `TRUST_POSTURE.md` exists precisely to let\noperators flip human gates from `block` to `auto`. Every gate flipped removes a human\nfrom the loop. Machine-level containment is what should backfill the removed human, and\nright now nothing does.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### New: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py`\n\nA pure, side-effect-free renderer. Takes a resolved isolation decision plus the\ncoordinator's network policy and worktree root; returns a runtime-specific policy\ndocument plus an argv wrapper.\n\n- `resolve_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode, ...) -> IsolationDecision` — consults\n  the task router when reachable, falls back to `get_agent_isolation()` from\n  `agents.yaml`, then to `none`. Mirrors the precedence ladder already established in\n  `environment_profile.py`.\n- `render_srt_settings(decision, worktree_root, network_policy) -> dict` — emits srt's\n  JSON settings shape: `allowWrite` scoped to the worktree root, `denyRead` covering\n  credential paths, `network.allowedDomains` from the coordinator's policy.\n- `wrap_command(cmd, decision) -> list[str]` — returns `cmd` unchanged when isolation is\n  not `sandbox` or the runtime is unavailable; otherwise returns the wrapped argv.\n\nThe renderer is deliberately runtime-shaped but not runtime-bound: `render_srt_settings`\nis one function beside a `render_*` seam, so an OpenShell YAML or container-args renderer\nis an addition rather than a rewrite. Both candidate runtimes are pre-1.0 (srt is a\n\"research preview\"; OpenShell is \"alpha — single-player mode\"), which makes the seam a\nrequirement rather than speculative generality.\n\n### Modified: `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`\n\n`CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()` and `dispatch_async()` call `wrap_command()` between\n`build_command()` and `subprocess.run()`. No other logic moves.\n\n### Modified: `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`\n\n`isolation_provided: bool` widens to a two-dimensional posture — filesystem and network\nisolation reported separately — because a container gives strong filesystem isolation and\nwide-open egress, and this change must be able to say \"skip the filesystem sandbox here,\nstill enforce the network allowlist.\"\n\nThe existing detection ladder also has a live bug: planning this change inside a cloud\nharness returned `isolation_provided=False source=default`, because the container exposes\nnone of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`. `worktree.py setup`\nconsequently attempted a real worktree and failed on the already-checked-out branch. The\nheuristic layer gains the missing signals.\n\nExisting `bool` callers keep working through a compatibility property; `worktree.py` and\n`merge_worktrees.py` read the filesystem dimension.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`\n\n`get_agent_isolation()` gains a companion that resolves *effective* isolation for an\n`(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair, so `review` and `alternative` can carry different\npostures under one agent entry — which `agents.yaml` already implies and cannot express.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`\n\nAn export path that serializes the active policy into the shape `sandbox_profile.py`\nconsumes. The policy stays authored in one place; enforcement becomes a rendering of it.\n\n### Degradation\n\nsrt requires macOS (Seatbelt) or Linux (bubblewrap + socat + ripgrep). When the runtime\nis absent or the platform is unsupported, dispatch **proceeds unsandboxed**, emits a\nwarning, and writes a coordinator audit event. This follows the degradation pattern\nalready used in `vendor_health.py`. Fail-closed would break every developer on an\nunsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense\nagainst confused agents rather than determined ones.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- **Sandbox lifecycle management in the coordinator.** No `sandbox_create` / `sandbox_destroy`\n  / connection brokering. That is OpenShell's entire product (a Rust gateway plus k3s); if\n  containerized isolation is needed later, dispatch should target OpenShell's API rather\n  than reimplementing a control plane. Related: `docker_manager.py` handles ParadeDB and\n  Colima lifecycle and must not grow into an agent sandbox manager — different problem,\n  different failure modes.\n- **Wrapping Bash inside skill scripts.** Many call sites, much broader blast radius,\n  deferred by explicit scope decision.\n- **Declaring the posture artifact.** `symphony/trust-posture-binding` owns declaration.\n  This change owns enforcement and consumes whatever that item declares.\n- **Protection against a determined exfiltrator.** See Trade-offs.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Approach 1 — OS-level wrapper at the dispatch chokepoint (**Recommended**)\n\nRender coordinator policy into an srt settings document and wrap the vendor argv in\n`CliVendorAdapter`.\n\n**Pros**\n- One injection site (`review_dispatcher.py:218` → `:279`) covers every current and\n  future vendor CLI, including vendors that ship no sandbox of their own.\n- Gives the existing advisory `network_policies.py` real teeth at the socket without\n  rewriting the policy model or moving where policy is authored.\n- Finally gives `isolation: sandbox` — already declared, validated, and tested — a\n  meaning, closing a gap the schema has advertised for some time.\n- srt is a single npm dependency with no daemon, no control plane, and no ops burden;\n  it is what Claude Code's own `/sandbox` uses.\n- Vendor-neutral: the same posture applies to `codex`, `gemini`, and any adapter added\n  later, rather than depending on each vendor's flags.\n\n**Cons**\n- Adds a Node dependency to a Python dispatch path.\n- Unsupported on Windows outside WSL2 (srt's Windows support is alpha).\n- OS-level sandboxing falls to a kernel bug; containers would be stronger.\n- srt is a research preview with an unstable interface.\n\n**Effort**: M\n\n### Approach 2 — Normalize vendor-native sandbox flags only\n\nDefine a portable mode vocabulary (`read-only`, `workspace-write`) and map it onto each\nvendor's own flags, extending what `agents.yaml` already does.\n\n**Pros**\n- No new dependency; works on every platform the vendor CLIs work on.\n- Smallest diff by a wide margin; effort S.\n- Zero risk of breaking dispatch on unsupported platforms.\n\n**Cons**\n- Enforces nothing we control — we are trusting each vendor's implementation, with no way\n  to verify it and no recourse when it is weak or absent.\n- Vendors without a sandbox mode get no protection at all.\n- Does not cover `SdkVendorAdapter`, which makes direct API calls with no CLI to flag.\n- Leaves `isolation: sandbox` still meaningless, and leaves `network_policies.py` still\n  advisory — neither of the two gaps that motivate this change actually closes.\n\n**Effort**: S\n\n### Approach 3 — Coordinator-managed container sandboxes (OpenShell or bespoke)\n\nGive the coordinator sandbox lifecycle primitives; run dispatched agents inside containers\nwith policy-enforced egress and injected credential providers.\n\n**Pros**\n- Strongest isolation boundary of the three; survives a kernel bug that defeats Seatbelt\n  or bubblewrap.\n- Credentials never touch the sandbox filesystem (OpenShell's provider model).\n- Handles the multi-tenant case this repo may eventually reach.\n\n**Cons**\n- Rebuilds, or takes a hard dependency on, an alpha \"single-player mode\" control plane.\n- Per-dispatch container startup latency against a review path that is currently a\n  subprocess spawn.\n- Substantial ops burden: image builds, registry, gateway lifecycle, k3s.\n- Overwhelmingly disproportionate to the threat model — the realistic failure is a\n  prompt-injected agent reading credentials, not a container escape.\n\n**Effort**: XL\n\n### Recommendation\n\n**Approach 1.** Approach 2 is cheaper but closes neither motivating gap: `isolation: sandbox`\nstays inert and network policy stays advisory, so it buys a vocabulary rather than a\ncontrol. Approach 3 buys a stronger boundary than the threat model needs, at the cost of\ndepending on an alpha control plane and adding container latency to every review dispatch.\n\nApproach 1 sits where the leverage is: one chokepoint, one dependency, enforcement of a\npolicy model that already exists. It also leaves Approach 3 open — `render_srt_settings`\nsits behind a seam, so adopting OpenShell later means adding a renderer, not redoing the\nintegration.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n**Accepted: containment of confused agents over containment of determined ones.** srt's own\ndocumentation is explicit that an allowlist containing `github.com` is an exfiltration\nchannel, that domain fronting works, and that an exposed Docker socket is a full escape.\nThis repository's workflow *requires* `github.com`. What this change buys is protection\nagainst accidental credential reads and unplanned egress. It is not a containment boundary\nagainst an adversary who knows GitHub is reachable, and the specs must not claim otherwise.\n\n**Accepted: a Node dependency in a Python path** over building OS-sandboxing bindings\nourselves.\n\n**Accepted: fail-open** over a hard guarantee, so unsupported platforms degrade instead of\nbreaking. The audit event is what makes the degradation visible rather than silent.\n\n## Impact\n\n- **Specs**: `agent-coordinator` (isolation resolution, policy export), `skill-workflow`\n  (dispatch wrapping), `worktree` (posture dimensions)\n- **Code**: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` (new), `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`,\n  `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`,\n  `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`\n- **Config**: `agents.yaml` per-mode isolation\n- **Docs**: `docs/guides/worktree-management.md` (posture, not bool)\n\n### Coordination with in-flight changes\n\n- **`implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model`** — `POST /route/task` returns\n  `isolation` among its outputs. That change is the **producer** of the decision; this one\n  is the **consumer**. `resolve_isolation()` calls the router when reachable. Because the\n  router change already specifies \"a local static fallback table when the coordinator is\n  down,\" this change is interface-bound to the router without being schedule-blocked by it:\n  the fallback is `get_agent_isolation()`, which exists today. The contract between them\n  must be pinned before either merges.\n- **`build-structured-vendor-result-channel`** — rewrites the same `CliVendorAdapter`\n  methods this change modifies. Direct merge-conflict risk; the two must not run\n  concurrently against `review_dispatcher.py`. Sequencing to be recorded in `design.md`.\n- **`add-coordinator-llm-gateway`** — same advisory-to-enforced argument applied to spend.\n  This change should follow its established shape rather than invent a parallel one.\n- **`symphony/trust-posture-binding`** — declaration layer. This change supplies the\n  enforcement its acceptance criterion (\"enforceable, not just documented\") requires.\n"}]},"isError":false}

Wrapping between those two points is what makes the control total; wrapping inside individual adapters would leave each new vendor unprotected by default.\n\n#### Scenario: Every vendor passes through the same seam\n\nWHEN any vendor CLI is dispatched, synchronously or asynchronously\nTHEN the constructed argv SHALL be passed through the wrapping seam before execution\nAND no adapter SHALL execute an argv that bypassed the seam.\n\n#### Scenario: Non-sandbox postures pass the argv through unchanged\n\nWHEN the resolved isolation decision is not `sandbox`\nTHEN the seam SHALL return the argv unchanged\nAND dispatch behavior SHALL be identical to dispatch before this change.\n\n### Requirement: The sandbox profile renderer SHALL be pure and runtime-seamed\n\nThe sandbox profile renderer SHALL be free of side effects, taking a resolved isolation decision together with the coordinator's network policy and the worktree root, and returning a runtime-specific policy document plus an argv wrapper.\n\nBoth candidate runtimes are pre-1.0, so the renderer SHALL expose a per-runtime rendering seam such that supporting an additional runtime is an addition rather than a rewrite.\n\n#### Scenario: Rendering performs no side effects\n\nWHEN the renderer is invoked\nTHEN it SHALL NOT mutate the filesystem, spawn a process, or contact the network\nAND the same inputs SHALL produce the same policy document.\n\n#### Scenario: Write scope is confined to the worktree root\n\nWHEN a policy document is rendered for a `sandbox` decision\nTHEN write access SHALL be scoped to the supplied worktree root\nAND read access SHALL be denied for credential paths\nAND permitted network destinations SHALL be taken from the coordinator's network policy.\n\n#### Scenario: A second runtime is added without rewriting the renderer\n\nWHEN support for an additional sandbox runtime is introduced\nTHEN it SHALL be added as an additional rendering function at the existing seam\nAND the resolution and wrapping logic SHALL remain unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: The authored network policy SHALL remain the single source of enforced destinations\n\nThe coordinator's network policy SHALL remain authored in one place, and enforcement SHALL be a rendering of that policy rather than a second, independently-maintained allowlist.\n\n#### Scenario: Enforced destinations derive from the authored policy\n\nWHEN a sandbox policy document is rendered\nTHEN its permitted network destinations SHALL be derived from the active coordinator network policy\nAND no destination SHALL be introduced that the authored policy does not permit.\n\n### Requirement: Unsupported platforms SHALL degrade openly rather than fail closed\n\nWhen the sandbox runtime is absent or the host platform is unsupported, dispatch SHALL proceed unsandboxed, SHALL emit a warning, and SHALL write a coordinator audit event recording that isolation was requested but not applied.\n\nFailing closed would break every developer on an unsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense against confused agents rather than determined ones. Degrading silently would be worse: an operator would believe a containment control was active when it was not.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing runtime degrades with a warning and an audit event\n\nWHEN the resolved isolation decision is `sandbox`\nAND the sandbox runtime is not installed or the platform is unsupported\nTHEN dispatch SHALL proceed without the sandbox\nAND a warning SHALL be emitted\nAND a coordinator audit event SHALL record that `sandbox` was requested and not applied.\n\n#### Scenario: Degradation is never silent\n\nWHEN dispatch proceeds unsandboxed after a `sandbox` decision\nTHEN the outcome SHALL be observable from the audit trail alone\nAND the dispatch SHALL NOT report itself as sandboxed.\n"}]},"isError":false}

Machine-level containment is what should backfill the removed human, and\nright now nothing does.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### New: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py`\n\nA pure, side-effect-free renderer. Takes a resolved isolation decision plus the\ncoordinator's network policy and worktree root; returns a runtime-specific policy\ndocument plus an argv wrapper.\n\n- `resolve_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode, ...) -> IsolationDecision` — consults\n  the task router when reachable, falls back to `get_agent_isolation()` from\n  `agents.yaml`, then to `none`. Mirrors the precedence ladder already established in\n  `environment_profile.py`.\n- `render_srt_settings(decision, worktree_root, network_policy) -> dict` — emits srt's\n  JSON settings shape: `allowWrite` scoped to the worktree root, `denyRead` covering\n  credential paths, `network.allowedDomains` from the coordinator's policy.\n- `wrap_command(cmd, decision) -> list[str]` — returns `cmd` unchanged when isolation is\n  not `sandbox` or the runtime is unavailable; otherwise returns the wrapped argv.\n\nThe renderer is deliberately runtime-shaped but not runtime-bound: `render_srt_settings`\nis one function beside a `render_*` seam, so an OpenShell YAML or container-args renderer\nis an addition rather than a rewrite. Both candidate runtimes are pre-1.0 (srt is a\n\"research preview\"; OpenShell is \"alpha — single-player mode\"), which makes the seam a\nrequirement rather than speculative generality.\n\n### Modified: `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`\n\n`CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()` and `dispatch_async()` call `wrap_command()` between\n`build_command()` and `subprocess.run()`. No other logic moves.\n\n### Modified: `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`\n\n`isolation_provided: bool` widens to a two-dimensional posture — filesystem and network\nisolation reported separately — because a container gives strong filesystem isolation and\nwide-open egress, and this change must be able to say \"skip the filesystem sandbox here,\nstill enforce the network allowlist.\"\n\nThe existing detection ladder also has a live bug: planning this change inside a cloud\nharness returned `isolation_provided=False source=default`, because the container exposes\nnone of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`. `worktree.py setup`\nconsequently attempted a real worktree and failed on the already-checked-out branch. The\nheuristic layer gains the missing signals.\n\nExisting `bool` callers keep working through a compatibility property; `worktree.py` and\n`merge_worktrees.py` read the filesystem dimension.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`\n\n`get_agent_isolation()` gains a companion that resolves *effective* isolation for an\n`(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair, so `review` and `alternative` can carry different\npostures under one agent entry — which `agents.yaml` already implies and cannot express.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`\n\nAn export path that serializes the active policy into the shape `sandbox_profile.py`\nconsumes. The policy stays authored in one place; enforcement becomes a rendering of it.\n\n### Degradation\n\nsrt requires macOS (Seatbelt) or Linux (bubblewrap + socat + ripgrep). When the runtime\nis absent or the platform is unsupported, dispatch **proceeds unsandboxed**, emits a\nwarning, and writes a coordinator audit event. This follows the degradation pattern\nalready used in `vendor_health.py`. Fail-closed would break every developer on an\nunsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense\nagainst confused agents rather than determined ones.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- **Sandbox lifecycle management in the coordinator.** No `sandbox_create` / `sandbox_destroy`\n  / connection brokering. That is OpenShell's entire product (a Rust gateway plus k3s); if\n  containerized isolation is needed later, dispatch should target OpenShell's API rather\n  than reimplementing a control plane. Related: `docker_manager.py` handles ParadeDB and\n  Colima lifecycle and must not grow into an agent sandbox manager — different problem,\n  different failure modes.\n- **Wrapping Bash inside skill scripts.** Many call sites, much broader blast radius,\n  deferred by explicit scope decision.\n- **Declaring the posture artifact.** `symphony/trust-posture-binding` owns declaration.\n  This change owns enforcement and consumes whatever that item declares.\n- **Protection against a determined exfiltrator.** See Trade-offs.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Approach 1 — OS-level wrapper at the dispatch chokepoint (**Recommended**)\n\nRender coordinator policy into an srt settings document and wrap the vendor argv in\n`CliVendorAdapter`.\n\n**Pros**\n- One injection site (`review_dispatcher.py:218` → `:279`) covers every current and\n  future vendor CLI, including vendors that ship no sandbox of their own.\n- Gives the existing advisory `network_policies.py` real teeth at the socket without\n  rewriting the policy model or moving where policy is authored.\n- Finally gives `isolation: sandbox` — already declared, validated, and tested — a\n  meaning, closing a gap the schema has advertised for some time.\n- srt is a single npm dependency with no daemon, no control plane, and no ops burden;\n  it is what Claude Code's own `/sandbox` uses.\n- Vendor-neutral: the same posture applies to `codex`, `gemini`, and any adapter added\n  later, rather than depending on each vendor's flags.\n\n**Cons**\n- Adds a Node dependency to a Python dispatch path.\n- Unsupported on Windows outside WSL2 (srt's Windows support is alpha).\n- OS-level sandboxing falls to a kernel bug; containers would be stronger.\n- srt is a research preview with an unstable interface.\n\n**Effort**: M\n\n### Approach 2 — Normalize vendor-native sandbox flags only\n\nDefine a portable mode vocabulary (`read-only`, `workspace-write`) and map it onto each\nvendor's own flags, extending what `agents.yaml` already does.\n\n**Pros**\n- No new dependency; works on every platform the vendor CLIs work on.\n- Smallest diff by a wide margin; effort S.\n- Zero risk of breaking dispatch on unsupported platforms.\n\n**Cons**\n- Enforces nothing we control — we are trusting each vendor's implementation, with no way\n  to verify it and no recourse when it is weak or absent.\n- Vendors without a sandbox mode get no protection at all.\n- Does not cover `SdkVendorAdapter`, which makes direct API calls with no CLI to flag.\n- Leaves `isolation: sandbox` still meaningless, and leaves `network_policies.py` still\n  advisory — neither of the two gaps that motivate this change actually closes.\n\n**Effort**: S\n\n### Approach 3 — Coordinator-managed container sandboxes (OpenShell or bespoke)\n\nGive the coordinator sandbox lifecycle primitives; run dispatched agents inside containers\nwith policy-enforced egress and injected credential providers.\n\n**Pros**\n- Strongest isolation boundary of the three; survives a kernel bug that defeats Seatbelt\n  or bubblewrap.\n- Credentials never touch the sandbox filesystem (OpenShell's provider model).\n- Handles the multi-tenant case this repo may eventually reach.\n\n**Cons**\n- Rebuilds, or takes a hard dependency on, an alpha \"single-player mode\" control plane.\n- Per-dispatch container startup latency against a review path that is currently a\n  subprocess spawn.\n- Substantial ops burden: image builds, registry, gateway lifecycle, k3s.\n- Overwhelmingly disproportionate to the threat model — the realistic failure is a\n  prompt-injected agent reading credentials, not a container escape.\n\n**Effort**: XL\n\n### Recommendation\n\n**Approach 1.** Approach 2 is cheaper but closes neither motivating gap: `isolation: sandbox`\nstays inert and network policy stays advisory, so it buys a vocabulary rather than a\ncontrol. Wrapping between those two points is what makes the control total; wrapping inside individual adapters would leave each new vendor unprotected by default.\n\n#### Scenario: Every vendor passes through the same seam\n\nWHEN any vendor CLI is dispatched, synchronously or asynchronously\nTHEN the constructed argv SHALL be passed through the wrapping seam before execution\nAND no adapter SHALL execute an argv that bypassed the seam.\n\n#### Scenario: Non-sandbox postures pass the argv through unchanged\n\nWHEN the resolved isolation decision is not `sandbox`\nTHEN the seam SHALL return the argv unchanged\nAND dispatch behavior SHALL be identical to dispatch before this change.\n\n### Requirement: The sandbox profile renderer SHALL be pure and runtime-seamed\n\nThe sandbox profile renderer SHALL be free of side effects, taking a resolved isolation decision together with the coordinator's network policy and the worktree root, and returning a runtime-specific policy document plus an argv wrapper.\n\nBoth candidate runtimes are pre-1.0, so the renderer SHALL expose a per-runtime rendering seam such that supporting an additional runtime is an addition rather than a rewrite.\n\n#### Scenario: Rendering performs no side effects\n\nWHEN the renderer is invoked\nTHEN it SHALL NOT mutate the filesystem, spawn a process, or contact the network\nAND the same inputs SHALL produce the same policy document.\n\n#### Scenario: Write scope is confined to the worktree root\n\nWHEN a policy document is rendered for a `sandbox` decision\nTHEN write access SHALL be scoped to the supplied worktree root\nAND read access SHALL be denied for credential paths\nAND permitted network destinations SHALL be taken from the coordinator's network policy.\n\n#### Scenario: A second runtime is added without rewriting the renderer\n\nWHEN support for an additional sandbox runtime is introduced\nTHEN it SHALL be added as an additional rendering function at the existing seam\nAND the resolution and wrapping logic SHALL remain unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: The authored network policy SHALL remain the single source of enforced destinations\n\nThe coordinator's network policy SHALL remain authored in one place, and enforcement SHALL be a rendering of that policy rather than a second, independently-maintained allowlist.\n\n#### Scenario: Enforced destinations derive from the authored policy\n\nWHEN a sandbox policy document is rendered\nTHEN its permitted network destinations SHALL be derived from the active coordinator network policy\nAND no destination SHALL be introduced that the authored policy does not permit.\n\n### Requirement: Unsupported platforms SHALL degrade openly rather than fail closed\n\nWhen the sandbox runtime is absent or the host platform is unsupported, dispatch SHALL proceed unsandboxed, SHALL emit a warning, and SHALL write a coordinator audit event recording that isolation was requested but not applied.\n\nFailing closed would Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement\n\n> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (item `dg-07`)\n> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`\n> Effort: M\n> Depends on: `dg-03` (isolation posture), `dg-06` (orchestrator obeys router)\n> Related: `symphony/trust-posture-binding` (priority 12) — declaration layer\n\n## Why\n\nThe coordinator has an `isolation` field that means nothing.\n\n`agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py:264` declares\n`VALID_ISOLATION_MODES = {\"worktree\", \"sandbox\", \"none\"}`. The value is schema-validated,\nstored on `AgentEntry`, exposed through `get_agent_isolation()` (`agents_config.py:979`),\nand asserted in `tests/test_agents_config_isolation.py:170` — which pins `codex` to\n`\"sandbox\"`. **No production caller reads it.** An agent declared `isolation: sandbox`\ntoday runs exactly like one declared `isolation: none`.\n\nThree adjacent gaps compound it:\n\n**Worktree isolation is concurrency isolation, not security isolation.** The invariant in\n`docs/guides/worktree-management.md` is rigorously enforced — one agent, one worktree, one\nbranch, guarded by `checkout_policy.py require-mutation`. It stops agents corrupting each\nother's git state. It does not stop a dispatched agent reading `~/.ssh/id_rsa` or POSTing\nthe repository to a pastebin, because a worktree is an ordinary directory owned by the\nordinary uid.\n\n**Network policy is advisory.** `network_policies.py` (90 lines) answers `check_domain()`\nthrough `policy_engine.py:361`. An agent must *voluntarily ask permission*. Nothing\nenforces the answer at the socket. This is the same defect `add-coordinator-llm-gateway`\nnames for spend: *\"that ceiling is advisory — enforced by post-hoc reconciliation, not at\nrequest time.\"* Same shape, different resource.\n\n**Sandbox intent is already expressed, in three incompatible dialects, enforced by nobody.**\n`agents.yaml:60-66` and `:131-137`:\n\n```yaml\nreview:      { args: [\"--print\", \"--allowedTools\", \"Read,Grep,Glob\"] }   # claude\nreview:      { args: [\"exec\", \"-s\", \"read-only\"] }                        # codex\nalternative: { args: [\"exec\", \"-s\", \"workspace-write\"] }\n```\n\nThe file's own header comment says \"the dispatch mode controls sandbox permissions.\" That\nis a policy statement per dispatch mode, written three different ways, enforced by whatever\neach vendor felt like implementing, verifiable by us in no way at all.\n\nMeanwhile `symphony/trust-posture-binding` commits to a posture artifact declaring\n\"sandbox mode, network allowlist\" bound to `policy_engine.py` so posture is\n\"**enforceable, not just documented**.\" There is currently no mechanism that could make\nit enforceable. This change is that mechanism.\n\n### Why now, and why at dispatch\n\nDispatched vendor CLIs are the sharpest edge in the system: `review_dispatcher.py`\nspawns `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` and friends with prompts assembled from repository\ncontent, and every one of them inherits the full ambient authority of the developer's\nuid — SSH keys, cloud credentials, shell rc files, unrestricted egress. That is code we\ndid not write, driven by prompts we do not fully review.\n\nIt is also, conveniently, a single chokepoint. `CliVendorAdapter.build_command()`\n(`review_dispatcher.py:218`) constructs `cmd`; `subprocess.run(cmd, ...)` at `:279` and\n`:521` executes it. One injection site covers every vendor.\n\nThe pressure is increasing, not static. `TRUST_POSTURE.md` exists precisely to let\noperators flip human gates from `block` to `auto`. Every gate flipped removes a human\nfrom the loop. Machine-level containment is what should backfill the removed human, and\nright now nothing does.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### New: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py`\n\nA pure, side-effect-free renderer. Takes a resolved isolation decision plus the\ncoordinator's network policy and worktree root; returns a runtime-specific policy\ndocument plus an argv wrapper.\n\n- `resolve_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode, ...) -> IsolationDecision` — consults\n  the task router when reachable, falls back to `get_agent_isolation()` from\n  `agents.yaml`, then to `none`. Mirrors the precedence ladder already established in\n  `environment_profile.py`.\n- `render_srt_settings(decision, worktree_root, network_policy) -> dict` — emits srt's\n  JSON settings shape: `allowWrite` scoped to the worktree root, `denyRead` covering\n  credential paths, `network.allowedDomains` from the coordinator's policy.\n- `wrap_command(cmd, decision) -> list[str]` — returns `cmd` unchanged when isolation is\n  not `sandbox` or the runtime is unavailable; otherwise returns the wrapped argv.\n\nThe renderer is deliberately runtime-shaped but not runtime-bound: `render_srt_settings`\nis one function beside a `render_*` seam, so an OpenShell YAML or container-args renderer\nis an addition rather than a rewrite. Both candidate runtimes are pre-1.0 (srt is a\n\"research preview\"; OpenShell is \"alpha — single-player mode\"), which makes the seam a\nrequirement rather than speculative generality.\n\n### Modified: `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`\n\n`CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()` and `dispatch_async()` call `wrap_command()` between\n`build_command()` and `subprocess.run()`. No other logic moves.\n\n### Modified: `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`\n\n`isolation_provided: bool` widens to a two-dimensional posture — filesystem and network\nisolation reported separately — because a container gives strong filesystem isolation and\nwide-open egress, and this change must be able to say \"skip the filesystem sandbox here,\nstill enforce the network allowlist.\"\n\nThe existing detection ladder also has a live bug: planning this change inside a cloud\nharness returned `isolation_provided=False source=default`, because the container exposes\nnone of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`. `worktree.py setup`\nconsequently attempted a real worktree and failed on the already-checked-out branch. The\nheuristic layer gains the missing signals.\n\nExisting `bool` callers keep working through a compatibility property; `worktree.py` and\n`merge_worktrees.py` read the filesystem dimension.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`\n\n`get_agent_isolation()` gains a companion that resolves *effective* isolation for an\n`(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair, so `review` and `alternative` can carry different\npostures under one agent entry — which `agents.yaml` already implies and cannot express.\n\n### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`\n\nAn export path that serializes the active policy into the shape `sandbox_profile.py`\nconsumes. The policy stays authored in one place; enforcement becomes a rendering of it.\n\n### Degradation\n\nsrt requires macOS (Seatbelt) or Linux (bubblewrap + socat + ripgrep). When the runtime\nis absent or the platform is unsupported, dispatch **proceeds unsandboxed**, emits a\nwarning, and writes a coordinator audit event. This follows the degradation pattern\nalready used in `vendor_health.py`. Fail-closed would break every developer on an\nunsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense\nagainst confused agents rather than determined ones.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- **Sandbox lifecycle management in the coordinator.** No `sandbox_create` / `sandbox_destroy`\n  / connection brokering. That is OpenShell's entire product (a Rust gateway plus k3s); if\n  containerized isolation is needed later, dispatch should target OpenShell's API rather\n  than reimplementing a control plane. Related: `docker_manager.py` handles ParadeDB and\n  Colima lifecycle and must not grow into an agent sandbox manager — different problem,\n  different failure modes.\n- **Wrapping Bash inside skill scripts.** Many call sites, much broader blast radius,\n  deferred by explicit scope decision.\n- **Declaring the posture artifact.** `symphony/trust-posture-binding` owns declaration.\n  This change owns enforcement and consumes whatever that item declares.\n- **Protection against a determined exfiltrator.** See Trade-offs.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Approach 1 — OS-level wrapper at the dispatch chokepoint (**Recommended**)\n\nRender coordinator policy into an srt settings document and wrap the vendor argv in\n`CliVendorAdapter`.\n\n**Pros**\n- One injection site (`review_dispatcher.py:218` → `:279`) covers every current and\n  future vendor CLI, including vendors that ship no sandbox of their own.\n- Gives the existing advisory `network_policies.py` real teeth at the socket without\n  rewriting the policy model or moving where policy is authored.\n- Finally gives `isolation: sandbox` — already declared, validated, and tested — a\n  meaning, closing a gap the schema has advertised for some time.\n- srt is a single npm dependency with no daemon, no control plane, and no ops burden;\n  it is what Claude Code's own `/sandbox` uses.\n- Vendor-neutral: the same posture applies to `codex`, `gemini`, and any adapter added\n  later, rather than depending on each vendor's flags.\n\n**Cons**\n- Adds a Node dependency to a Python dispatch path.\n- Unsupported on Windows outside WSL2 (srt's Windows support is alpha).\n- OS-level sandboxing falls to a kernel bug; containers would be stronger.\n- srt is a research preview with an unstable interface.\n\n**Effort**: M\n\n### Approach 2 — Normalize vendor-native sandbox flags only\n\nDefine a portable mode vocabulary (`read-only`, `workspace-write`) and map it onto each\nvendor's own flags, extending what `agents.yaml` already does.\n\n**Pros**\n- No new dependency; works on every platform the vendor CLIs work on.\n- Smallest diff by a wide margin; effort S.\n- Zero risk of breaking dispatch on unsupported platforms.\n\n**Cons**\n- Enforces nothing we control — we are trusting each vendor's implementation, with no way\n  to verify it and no recourse when it is weak or absent.\n- Vendors without a sandbox mode get no protection at all.\n- Does not cover `SdkVendorAdapter`, which makes direct API calls with no CLI to flag.\n- Leaves `isolation: sandbox` still meaningless, and leaves `network_policies.py` still\n  advisory — neither of the two gaps that motivate this change actually closes.\n\n**Effort**: S\n\n### Approach 3 — Coordinator-managed container sandboxes (OpenShell or bespoke)\n\nGive the coordinator sandbox lifecycle primitives; run dispatched agents inside containers\nwith policy-enforced egress and injected credential providers.\n\n**Pros**\n- Strongest isolation boundary of the three; survives a kernel bug that defeats Seatbelt\n  or bubblewrap.\n- Credentials never touch the sandbox filesystem (OpenShell's provider model).\n- Handles the multi-tenant case this repo may eventually reach.\n\n**Cons**\n- Rebuilds, or takes a hard dependency on, an alpha \"single-player mode\" control plane.\n- Per-dispatch container startup latency against a review path that is currently a\n  subprocess spawn.\n- Substantial ops burden: image builds, registry, gateway lifecycle, k3s.\n- Overwhelmingly disproportionate to the threat model — the realistic failure is a\n  prompt-injected agent reading credentials, not a container escape.\n\n**Effort**: XL\n\n### Recommendation\n\n**Approach 1.** Approach 2 is cheaper but closes neither motivating gap: `isolation: sandbox`\nstays inert and network policy stays advisory, so it buys a vocabulary rather than a\ncontrol. Approach 3 buys a stronger boundary than the threat model needs, at the cost of\ndepending on an alpha control plane and adding container latency to every review dispatch.\n\nApproach 1 sits where the leverage is: one chokepoint, one dependency, enforcement of a\npolicy model that already exists. It also leaves Approach 3 open — `render_srt_settings`\nsits behind a seam, so adopting OpenShell later means adding a renderer, not redoing the\nintegration.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n**Accepted: containment of confused agents over containment of determined ones.** srt's own\ndocumentation is explicit that an allowlist containing `github.com` is an exfiltration\nchannel, that domain fronting works, and that an exposed Docker socket is a full escape.\nThis repository's workflow *requires* `github.com`. What this change buys is protection\nagainst accidental credential reads and unplanned egress. It is not a containment boundary\nagainst an adversary who knows GitHub is reachable, and the specs must not claim otherwise.\n\n**Accepted: a Node dependency in a Python path** over building OS-sandboxing bindings\nourselves.\n\n**Accepted: fail-open** over a hard guarantee, so unsupported platforms degrade instead of\nbreaking. The audit event is what makes the degradation visible rather than silent.\n\n## Impact\n\n- **Specs**: `agent-coordinator` (isolation resolution, policy export), `skill-workflow`\n  (dispatch wrapping), `worktree` (posture dimensions)\n- **Code**: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` (new), `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`,\n  `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`,\n  `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`\n- **Config**: `agents.yaml` per-mode isolation\n- **Docs**: `docs/guides/worktree-management.md` (posture, not bool)\n\n### Coordination with in-flight changes\n\n- **`implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model`** — `POST /route/task` returns\n  `isolation` among its outputs. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading + validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at        poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n                        command_template=raw_poll[\"command_template\"],\n                        result_protocol=raw_poll[\"result_protocol\"],\n                        interval_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n model_flag=raw_cli[\"model_flag\"],\n                model=raw_cli.get(\"model\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_cli.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. Migration 022 granted the merge\n#: queue operations with ``WHERE trust_level >= 3`` — no capability in\n#: ``agents.yaml`` covers them, so the projection needs this second dimension\n#: to reproduce the grants the migrations made.\nTRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS: tuple[tuple[int, tuple[str, ...]], ...] = (\n    (\n        int(TrustLevel.ELEVATED),\n        (\n            \"register_feature\",\n            \"deregister_feature\",\n            \"enqueue_merge\",\n            \"run_pre_merge_checks\",\n            \"mark_merged\",\n            \"remove_from_merge_queue\",\n            \"publish_work_projection\",\n            \"report_vendor_rate_limit\",\n        ),\n    ),\n)\n\n#: Profile rows the registry deliberately does NOT own (design D2 amendment).\n#:\n#: ``agents.yaml`` describes *harness identities*: things that can be\n#: dispatched, that speak a transport, and that authenticate. Some profile rows\n#: describe a *role* instead — ``evaluator`` (migration 026_evaluator_profile)\n#: is the generator/evaluator split's read-only reviewer role, has no CLI and no\n#: transport, and could never be given an ``agents.yaml`` entry without the\n#: registry claiming to describe an agent it cannot dispatch. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading + validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n    Args:\n        path: Path to agents YAML file.\n        secrets_path: Path to ``.secrets.yaml`` for ``${VAR}`` interpolation\n            in ``api_key`` fields.\n\n    Returns:\n        List of validated :class:`AgentEntry` objects.\n\n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If *path* does not exist.\n        jsonschema.ValidationError: If the data fails schema validation.\n        ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n                        command_template=raw_poll[\"command_template\"],\n                        result_protocol=raw_poll[\"result_protocol\"],\n                        interval_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n                    )\n                return ModeConfig(\n                    args=mode_data[\"args\"],\n                    async_dispatch=mode_data.get(\"async\", False),\n                    isolation=mode_data.get(\"isolation\"),\n                    poll=poll_config,\n                )\n\n            cli_config = CliConfig(\n                command=raw_cli[\"command\"],\n model_flag=raw_cli[\"model_flag\"],\n                model=raw_cli.get(\"model\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_cli.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n                prompt_via_stdin=raw_cli.get(\"prompt_via_stdin\", False),\n                prompt_via_flag=raw_cli.get(\"prompt_via_flag\", \"\"),\n                api_key_env=raw_cli.get(\"api_key_env\", \"\"),\n            )\n\n        sdk_config: SdkConfig | None = None\n        raw_sdk = agent_data.get(\"sdk\")\n        if raw_sdk:\n            sdk_config = SdkConfig(\n                package=raw_sdk[\"package\"],\n                model=raw_sdk[\"model\"],\n                method=raw_sdk.get(\"method\", \"messages.create\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_sdk.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n                api_key_env=raw_sdk.get(\"api_key_env\", \"\"),\n                max_tokens=raw_sdk.get(\"max_tokens\", 16384),\n api_key=resolved_key,\n                openbao_role_id=agent_data.get(\"openbao_role_id\"),\n                endpoint_kind=agent_data.get(\"endpoint_kind\"),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``.
